title: Indefinite Expressions
description: Learn algo, alguien, alguno, nada, nadie, nunca, siempre and other indefinite expressions in Spanish.

grammar.title: Algo, Alguien, Alguno — Something, Someone, Some
grammar.content:
Positive indefinite expressions (something, someone, some):

algo (something/anything):
Algo paso. (Something happened.)
Quieres algo? (Do you want something?)
Algo de agua (some water)

alguien (someone/somebody):
Alguien llama a la puerta. (Someone is knocking on the door.)
Hay alguien ahi? (Is someone there?)

alguno/algunos/al guna/algunas (some/any):
Tengo algunos libros. (I have some books.)
Alguna pregunta? (Any question?)
Algunas personas vienen. (Some people are coming.)

Note: Alguno becomes algún before masculine singular nouns:
Algún problema? (Any problem?)
Ningún (none/no) is the negative form:
No tengo ningún problema. (I don't have any problem.)
examples: Alguien te busca. (Someone is looking for you.)
Tengo algunas ideas. (I have some ideas.)
Ningún problema, todo esta bien. (No problem, everything is fine.)

grammar.title: Nada, Nadie, Ninguno — Nothing, No One, None
grammar.content:
Negative indefinite expressions:

nada (nothing/anything):
No veo nada. (I don't see anything. / I see nothing.)
Nada me importa. (Nothing matters to me.)

nadie (no one/nobody):
Nadie vino a la fiesta. (No one came to the party.)
No hay nadie en casa. (There's nobody home.)

ninguno/ninguna (none/no one):
Ninguno de ellos sabe. (None of them know.)
No tengo ninguna idea. (I have no idea.)

Ninguno contracts to ningún before masc singular nouns:
Ningún problema. (No problem.)

Double negatives in Spanish:
No hay nadie = There is nobody (standard)
Nadie hay = Nobody there (ungrammatical in standard Spanish)

With 'si' clause:
Si alguien llama, dime. (If someone calls, tell me.)
examples: Nada me hace feliz. (Nothing makes me happy.)
Nadie sabe la respuesta. (Nobody knows the answer.)
Ninguno de los dos vino. (Neither of the two came.)
No tengo ningún interés. (I have no interest.)

grammar.title: Todo, Siempre, Nunca — Everything, Always, Never
grammar.content:
todo (all/every/everything):
Todo está bien. (Everything is fine.)
Todos los días. (Every day. / All days.)
Todas las personas vinieron. (All the people came.)

siempre (always):
Siempre llego tarde. (I'm always late.)
Para siempre. (Forever.)

nunca/jamás (never):
Nunca he estado en París. (I've never been to Paris.)
Jamás pense eso. (I never thought that.)

jamás is more emphatic than nunca:
Nunca me lo dijo. (He never told me.)
Jamás me lo diría. (I would never tell him.)

también (also/too) vs. tampoco (neither/not either):
Yo también quiero ir. (I also want to go.)
Yo tampoco quiero ir. (I don't want to go either.)
examples: Todo el mundo quiere ser feliz. (Everyone wants to be happy.)
Siempre te recordare. (I will always remember you.)
A mi también me gusta. (I like it too. / I also like it.)

pronunciation.title: Indefinite Expressions Pronunciation
pronunciation.content:
algo = AL-goh (something)
alguien = AL-gee-en (someone)
alguno = al-GOO-noh (some)
nada = NAH-dah (nothing)
nadie = NAH-dee-eh (no one)
ninguno = neen-GOO-noh (none)
todo = TOH-doh (all/everything)
siempre = see-EM-preh (always)
nunca = NOON-kah (never)
jamás = hah-MAHS (never)
también = tahm-BEEN (also)
tampoco = tahm-POH-koh (neither)
cada = KAH-dah (each/every)
cualquiera = kwal-KEE-eh-rah (any/whoever)

Key pronunciation notes:
- alguien ends with -en sound, not -iente
- jamás has stress on second syllable
- también and tampoco both have -mp- sound

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'Someone is calling'?
exercises.explanation: Alguien = someone/somebody. Algo = something. Nada = nothing. Nadie = no one.

exercises.question: Complete: 'No veo ___. (I don't see anything.)'
exercises.explanation: Nada = nothing/anything (negative). 'No veo nada' = I don't see anything / I see nothing.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I have no idea' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: Ninguna idea = no idea. With negation, use 'ninguna' (not 'alguna').

exercises.question: Complete: '___ los dias voy al gimnasio. (Every day I go to the gym.)'
exercises.explanation: Todos los dias = every day/all days. 'Todos' agrees with 'dias' (masculine plural).

exercises.question: Which is correct for 'I will always love you'?
exercises.explanation: Siempre = always. Future tense: 'Te amare' = I will love you.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ he estado en Roma. (I have never been in Rome.)'
exercises.explanation: Nunca = never. Present perfect: 'Nunca he estado' = I have never been.

exercises.question: How do you say 'I also want to go' in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: También = also/too. 'Yo también quiero ir' = I also want to go.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Creo que ___. (I think so / I don't think so)'
exercises.explanation: Affirmative: 'Creo que sí' (I think so). Negative: 'Creo que no' (I don't think so).

exercises.question: Which is NOT a negative indefinite expression?
exercises.explanation: Alguno is positive (some/any). Nada, nadie, and ningun are all negative.

exercises.question: Complete: '___ problema. (No problem.)'
exercises.explanation: Ningún = no (contracted form before masculine singular noun). Full: Ningún problema.
